utilities.note: Residential slab tariff. Charges rise as monthly consumption crosses each slab.

accessibility.headline: Free parking permit for People of Determination
accessibility.detail: A permanent People of Determination permit is free, covers up to five linked vehicles, lasts three years, and lets you park anywhere in Dubai. There's a temporary version for up to a year if you're recovering from something, and a tourist permit valid for sixty days. Applications go through the Parkin app or website, and you normally hear back within three working days.

accessibility.headline: Free travel on the Metro and public buses
accessibility.detail: With a personalised People of Determination nol card you travel free on the Dubai Metro and public buses, and intercity buses too. The card costs seventy dirhams — fifty for the card itself and twenty loaded on as credit for things it doesn't cover, like the water bus and parking. It lasts five years, and you can renew it on the same terms.

accessibility.headline: Salik toll exemption for one vehicle
accessibility.detail: People of Determination can have one vehicle exempted from Salik road tolls. The exemption is renewed every year.

accessibility.headline: Wheelchair-accessible taxis, around the clock
accessibility.detail: Dubai Taxi runs a fleet of accessible taxis twenty-four hours a day covering the whole emirate, with wheelchair lifts, a wheelchair on board, seating for a companion, and drivers trained for it. You're charged the same fare as any other taxi.
accessibility.provider: Dubai Taxi, Roads and Transport Authority

accessibility.headline: Step-free Metro with wheelchair spaces on every carriage
accessibility.detail: Every Metro station has tactile guide paths for visually impaired passengers, lifts sized for wheelchairs, step-free routes from the car park, and accessible toilets. Each carriage has a dedicated wheelchair space right by the door. There are audio announcements for visually impaired passengers and screens for those who are hard of hearing, and ticket booths are built at wheelchair height.

accessibility.headline: Low-floor buses across the network
accessibility.detail: Dubai's public buses are low-floor so you can board without steps, with request buttons within reach from a seated position and air-conditioned shelters at the stops.

accessibility.headline: Water buses and ferries take wheelchairs
accessibility.detail: The water bus has space for up to three wheelchairs and the Dubai Ferry for two, with foldable seating to make room. Marine stations are designed for step-free access, and there's a crew member at each marina to help you board.

accessibility.headline: Priority service at RTA centres
accessibility.detail: RTA customer service centres have fast-track queues and dedicated counters for People of Determination, with accessible parking by the main entrance. The main ones are at Umm Ramool, and the licensing departments in Deira and Al Barsha.

accessibility.headline: Vehicle adaptation and licensing support
accessibility.detail: RTA's licensing arm will advise you on the adaptations a vehicle needs, point you to companies that fit them, and then test and formally endorse the vehicle as adapted for a driver who is a Person of Determination.

accessibility.headline: Free parking near a hospital during treatment
accessibility.detail: If you're visiting a hospital regularly for treatment there's a special medical permit that gives you free parking in paid public spaces within five hundred metres of the facility, for as long as you need it.
